Subject: General

Topic 5.1: Observing and Articulating signs (listening and speaking) 5.1.2 Auditory discrimination Visual discrimination
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating signs (listening and speaking) 5.1.2 Auditory discrimination Visual discrimination, part of MY NEIGHBORHOOD Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning  in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: What are the common sounds in the environment? 2. How do you respond to different sounds in the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating signs (listening and speaking) 5.1.2 Auditory discrimination Visual discrimination together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Love: Hospitability as learner appreciates one another in imitating familiar sounds.

● Responsibility: as learner becomes aware of different things producing sounds in the environment and appreciate what the

sounds communicate.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
60

• Disaster Risk Reduction awareness as the learner learns that some sounds in the environment communicate danger and the need

to take precaution.

• Socio-economic issues awareness as learner learns that some sounds from the environment result from economic activities like

sounds of posho mills, vehicles in business.

Link to other Learning Areas :

• Religious education as learners appreciate different sounds made within the environment.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as hearing aids and amplifiers,Realia, signed audi visual recordings,

relevant digital devices, online resources, tools that produce vibrations to help the child feel the sound such as a drum, a tuning fork,

or a speaker placed on a resonating surface.
